page.layout: One page of text, no margin notes. Running head at top with the page number 354 beside it. Heading "ARTICVLVS QVARTVS." with subtitle "De Meteoris Aëreis.", then a paragraph 1, a heading "D.E. IRIDE.", paragraphs 2 to 4 in one column, and at the foot the catchword "5. Cæte-".

main_text.head: ARTICULUS QUARTUS.
De Meteoris Aëreis.
main_text.p: 1. Meteora aërea vulgò ponuntur ista, Iris, ventus, vorago, hiatus, halo, parclius[?], & parasclene[?].
main_text.head: D.E. IRIDE.
main_text.p: 2. Iris est arcus multicolor in nube rorida, concava, & opaca, ex radiorum solarium reflexione apparens; quæ definitio comprehendit causam efficientem & materialem Iridis. Causa enim efficiens Iri-dis est Sol vibrans radios in nubem: Causa vero materialis est nubes rorida recipiens solares radios. Fit autem Iris vulgò, quando Sol emittit radios in nubem roridam & diaphanam in parte inferiori, & opacam in parte superiori; ex eo enim quòd nubes sit ita disposita fit ut recipiat lucem Solis, quam reflectit ad nos ob quandam opacitatem, quæ radiis solaribus non penetratur.

3. Lux intercepta intra nubem nobis repræsentat diversos colores: Cum enim nubes in suprema parte sit crassior, eâ parte colorem purpureum & rubrum refert; nam lumen permixtum exhalationi nigræ & densæ re-fert rubrum colorem, ut patet in carbone accenso, & aliis similibus; medius color nobis apparet viridis, eò quòd nubes in medio rarior sit, quàm in summo, ultimus verò color apparet cæruleus, quia nubes in inferiori parte rarior est quàm in medio & summo: Alii addunt colorem flavum, & alios minùs præcipuos. Scaliger existimavit nubem constare ex omnium elementorum particulis, & supremas excipientes lucem rutilare tanquam igneas, sequentes flavescere tanquam aëreas, tertias virescere tanquam aqueas, extremas fieri cæruleas & nigricantes tanquam terreas.

4. Figura Iridis est circularis aut in arcum; quia radii Solis à corpore Solis tanquam à centro aut quasi centro diffunduntur æqualiter per lineam rectam; hoc enim habent omnia corpora luminosa, ut ab unoquoque sui puncto emittant radios per lineas rectas æqualiter; ex quo sequitur, ut radii omnes simul qui procedunt à corpore luminoso semper desinant in circulum aut semicirculum; non quòd radii singuli efficiant circulum aut semicirculum, cum singuli terminentur puncto, sed quòd linea quæ ducitur ab extremis punctis lineatum sit semper circularis aut in arcum.

page.notes: Doubtful readings: "parclius" and "parasclene" in paragraph 1 are read with [?] because the small print makes the letters e/c and the second vowel unclear. The large initial M of "Meteora" and the initial I of "Iris" are taken as the first letter of the word. Dotted spaced capitals in the running head and "D.E. IRIDE." are normalised to plain capitals and spacing. The catchword "5. Cæte-" is kept as printed and ends with a hyphen. The digitiser's mark at the bottom right is omitted. The printed "lineatum" in paragraph 4 is left as printed.
